summary.oneLiner: Integra Engineering India Limited (IEIL) designs, manufactures and supplies engineered solutions for the industrial and transportation sectors, with a primary focus on railway and rolling stock applications for OEMs in India and select global markets.
summary.business: IEIL's core areas of expertise include sheet metal fabrication, wiring and electromechanical solutions, and aluminium metro interior systems, supported by in-house CNC laser cutting, punching, precision bending, welding and surface finishing capabilities. In the rolling stock segment it supplies aluminium metro interior components such as ceilings, side walls, side window panels, door pillars, end walls, saloon doors and complete driver cab interiors to OEMs, alongside wiring harness design, control panel assembly and functional testing. currentContext.business: IEIL's core areas of expertise include sheet metal fabrication, wiring and electromechanical solutions, and aluminium metro interior systems, supported by in-house CNC laser cutting, punching, precision bending, welding and surface finishing capabilities. In the rolling stock segment it supplies aluminium metro interior components such as ceilings, side walls, side window panels, door pillars, end walls, saloon doors and complete driver cab interiors to OEMs, alongside wiring harness design, control panel assembly and functional testing. During the year the Company increased its focus on higher value-added assemblies and system-level supplies in addition to standalone component manufacturing.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated solution provider spanning sheet metal fabrication, wiring/electromechanical assembly and aluminium metro interior systems, allowing multi-stage value-chain offerings rather than single-component supply|In-house manufacturing capabilities (CNC laser cutting, punching, precision bending, welding, surface finishing) enabling customer-specific technical and quality requirements|Multiple international process and product certifications (EN 15085, EN 17460/TBBCert, AWS welder qualification) that act as qualification barriers for export customers, particularly in the USA and Europe|Machinery is not segment-specific and can be redeployed for contract manufacturing in other industries, providing flexibility against rolling-stock demand swings|Established relationships with key OEM customers with expanding scope in existing projects
currentContext.strategies: Expand presence in rolling stock and metro projects with various OEMs|Increase share in export markets|Enhance capabilities in system integration and assemblies|Build design and development capabilities in-house and with partnerships|Improve operational efficiency through automation and digitalization|Maximize utilization of newly added capacities|Strengthen capabilities as an integrated solution provider, with increased focus on higher value-added assemblies and system-level supplies in addition to standalone component manufacturing|Focus on both domestic and export markets to accommodate shifts in regional demand, using non-segment-specific machinery that can also serve contract manufacturing for other industries
currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26, the Company reported progress in infrastructure expansion including additional production facilities, continued investment in new machinery and automation initiatives, and improvement in production efficiency through process optimization and capacity enhancement. No specific project name, site, capacity quantum or commissioning timeline is disclosed in this bundle; the Outlook section states the Company intends to 'maximize utilization of newly added capacities' going forward.
currentContext.mdna: Outlook remains positive, supported by strong demand in the railway and metro segments|Robust order pipeline and ongoing infrastructure investments in the railway sector expected to drive steady and sustainable growth|Indian railway rolling stock market (2026-2036) entering its largest modernisation and expansion cycle since independence, driven by government capex, 'Make in India' indigenous manufacturing, rapid expansion of Vande Bharat and semi-high-speed trains, metro rail growth in Tier 2 cities, rail electrification and green mobility, export opportunities, automation/digital manufacturing adoption, and a shift towards modular and lightweight designs|Record railway capital expenditure allocation from the Government of India (Union Budget 2026-27 approx. Rs. 2.93 lakh crore, the highest ever) presents strong long-term growth opportunities for the Company|Global railway industry transformation driven by sustainability, digitalisation, urbanisation and modernisation - green mobility transition, smart infrastructure/digital signalling, AI-driven predictive maintenance, network/fleet modernisation, and an Asia-Pacific urban transit boom|Opportunities: expansion in the Vande Bharat train ecosystem, growth in the metro rail interior segment, increasing demand for localized manufacturing, export opportunities to Europe and other global markets, and transition towards integrated system supply|Threats: dependence on OEM customers and project-based demand, margin pressure from competitive pricing, availability of skilled manpower, and supply chain disruptions/raw material price fluctuations|With a robust order pipeline and ongoing infrastructure investments in the railway sector, the Company expects steady and sustainable growth in the coming years.

risks.note: Volatility in prices of raw materials (sheet metal) can impact margins; the Company has price variance clauses with most, but not all, customers, so exposure remains for uncovered contracts.
Production planning and schedules vary with labour fluctuation, impacting on-time delivery of projects; mitigated via hiring from ITI, welding training and a dedicated Welding Training Center.

risks.risk: Dependency on the rolling stock market
risks.note: A sudden drop in demand for public transport solutions could significantly impact turnover and profitability; the Company is diversifying via domestic and export markets, and its machinery is not segment-specific so it can be redeployed for contract manufacturing in other industries.

risks.risk: Dependence on OEM customers and project-based demand
risks.note: Flagged as a threat in the MD&A - revenue is concentrated among a limited set of OEM customers and tied to lumpy, project-based order flow.
Flagged as a threat - pricing competition in the industry can compress margins.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruptions and raw material price fluctuations
risks.note: Flagged as a threat separate from sheet metal-specific volatility - broader supply chain disruption risk affecting input availability and cost.
